findings.location: architecture/w03-obligation-amendment-1/README.md:31-32; amendment.json changes[2].source, changes[3].source and the HE-003 shares
findings.finding: This is what remains of R3-5. The README and both `source` fields say that the HE-002S design 'is published with the HE-002S pull request', but nothing schedules that. The design's packet (§8) lists no design path, and its flow (§9) has no publication step. In the precedents, HE-002B's PR body (18 lines) and HE-002C's PR body (97 lines) do not carry their designs. Several parts of the shares come from that design and from no owner decision: `kept` derived from the I04 port, the distinct exit status, the accepted start states, the /proc/self reads, the gate staying dumpable on HE-008's side, and RUST_BACKTRACE (design §2, §5, §6). They are cited only to 'the HE-002S design', with no section, although R3-5 asked for §2 and §6. The HE-003 shares now end with one collective citation '(Q-HE2S-4, Q-HE2S-5, Q-HE2S-7, Q-HE2S-8)'. That covers the stage content, but it also covers the exit-status clause and the I04 clause, which come from the design. I compared the share texts with design revision 3 §2, §5, §6 and §14-§16, and they are faithful to it.
findings.requiredChange: Record the publication in the HE-002S design (§8 or §9), for example the PR body carries §2, §5 and §6, or the design is added at a stated path. Otherwise, word the README as an intent ('is to be published'). Add the design sections to the two `source` fields: §2 for the start states, preconditions and stages; §5 for RUST_BACKTRACE; §6 for the HE-003 carry. No owner decision is needed.

findings.finding: The README marks only Q-HE2S-7 as amending Q-HE2S-4. Q-HE2S-8 also amends it. Read verbatim, Q-HE2S-4 puts no_new_privs in stage 2 ('Stage 2: drop to {kept}, no_new_privs, then the filter'), while the HE-003 shares put it in stage 1, as Q-HE2S-8 ('move no_new_privs into stage 1') requires. The record is consistent because Q-HE2S-8 is carried verbatim beside Q-HE2S-4. Design §2 states the relation in full: 'Q-HE2S-4 (a), amended by Q-HE2S-7 (a) and Q-HE2S-8 (a)'.
findings.requiredChange: In the README, say that both decisions amend Q-HE2S-4. For example: 'Q-HE2S-7 (the gate stays dumpable) and Q-HE2S-8 (no_new_privs in stage 1, a second thread check), both amending Q-HE2S-4'.

findings.finding: Two points about HE-008's shares, neither of which leaves an ownership gap. (1) SEC-4's share, 'the unit uses no systemd seccomp option (W02d's carried F10)', restates plan v2 obligation SEC-3. SEC-3 reads 'No systemd seccomp options on planeon units.', has packets [HE-008], and its source is seccomp-allowlists-v2/status.json:95, which is 'no systemd seccomp options (F10)'. The share does not name SEC-3, so a reader or the mechanics layer could count F10 as a second obligation. (2) HI-7's share calls its list 'a start state the seal accepts (the full root set, or one already reduced within {CAP_SETPCAP, CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE} ...)'. Design §2 also accepts 'any superset of the targets below', so the list reads narrower than the seal's acceptance. As an obligation on HE-008 the narrower list is conservative, and the rest of the parenthetical is equivalent to design §2: the permitted set holds `kept`, and nothing is left to drop without CAP_SETPCAP.
findings.requiredChange: Write SEC-4's HE-008 share as '... no systemd seccomp option (plan v2 SEC-3, W02d's F10) ...'. Then either add 'or any superset of that target' to HI-7's start-state list, or say that HE-008 starts the gate in one of the listed states. The README rows follow.

dispositions.evidence: README.md lines 12-18 form one table: the header 'Obligation | Change | Packets | Text, ownership or share', the delimiter, and the rows I07-6, I07-4, SEC-4, HI-7 and SEC-QW4, in that order with no blank line. Every row has four cells. A blank line 19 ends the table. The checker confirms this (tab lines contiguous, 7 lines).

Fix (1) was taken. SEC-4 has packetsAdded [HE-003, HE-008] and packets [HE-002S, HE-003, HE-004, HE-005, HE-006, HE-007, HE-008], which is plan v2's list plus the two added packets in plan v2's packet order. Both added packets have shares. HI-7 has packetsAdded [HE-003] and shares for HE-003 and HE-008. README:28-30 states the literal reading: 'HE-003 and HE-008 are added to SEC-4, and HE-003 to HI-7, which already lists HE-008'. That matches the scope decision and design §4, 'SEC-4 and HI-7 add HE-003 (...) and HE-008 (...)'. The HE-008 elements are split between the two obligations. SEC-4 gets F10 and the start state; HI-7 gets the uid, the start state, SELinux and the core items. The SEC-4 install step also depends on HI-7's uid/gid 0 and SELinux self-permissions, but HE-008 owns them there, so there is no gap. On F10, see R4-3.

Both HE-003 shares (they are identical) and README:20-25 now say that HE-003 'derives kept from it (CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE exactly when the signed I04 port is below 1024, else nothing) and passes it to stage 2'. This matches design §2 ('Between the stages ... yields `kept` ... HE-002S's API takes `kept` as a value') and HOST_INTERFACE_SPEC.md:405. HE-008's HI-7 share says 'uid 0 and gid 0', which matches design §2's getresuid/getresgid precondition. The README paragraph equals the JSON share without its decision citation; the checker compared them after backtick and whitespace normalisation.

`shareRule` and README:34-38 state that 'A share adds to the named packet's part of the obligation as plan v2 states it; it never narrows it', and that an obligation's text is unchanged by PACKETS_ADDED. The SEC-QW4 quotation 'steady state is W02d v3 and T04' is an exact substring of plan v2's SEC-QW4 text. The second rule I asked for, that a listed packet without a share keeps its plan v2 part, is not stated in words. It follows from 'adds ... never narrows' together with `unchanged`. The schema check in the mechanics layer is carried to the mechanics, which are not under review.

Q-HE2S-4, Q-HE2S-5, Q-HE2S-7 and Q-HE2S-8 are now in `ownerDecisions`. Under whitespace normalisation each equals its design line: Q-HE2S-4 and Q-HE2S-5 in §14, Q-HE2S-7 and Q-HE2S-8 in §15. Q-HE2S-3 (§11) and the scope decision (§14) are also still verbatim. The B-ids are gone from `source`, and the record says where the design becomes public. Two parts remain open: the design sections are not cited, and the publication is not scheduled anywhere. Both are carried as R4-1.

HE-003's share now covers nnp in stage 1 (Q-HE2S-8), the second single-thread check at the start of stage 2 (Q-HE2S-8), and the source check over the code between the stages (Q-HE2S-8, design §6). Its stage-1 list has no dumpable step (Q-HE2S-7), and its 'at most' matches design §2's '∩ start bounding/permitted'. HE-008's HI-7 share covers the following, as design §2 'Start state', 'Preconditions' and 'Out', §5 (C8) and Q-HE2S-7 state them: the accepted start states (C2); the gate staying dumpable; core_pattern not a pipe or its helper honouring RLIMIT_CORE 0 (Q-HE2S-7's own carry to HE-008); RUST_BACKTRACE unset; capability setpcap; process setcap, getcap and setrlimit; dir search and file open and read for /proc/self/status (C4); and no process setrlimit on other domains. On precision, see R4-3 (2).
